goal: Evaluate whether the target model can inspect a tiny Python repository in a sandbox, run tests, and fix a failing bug.

spec.objective: Evaluate whether the target model can inspect a tiny Python repository in a sandbox, run tests, and fix a failing bug by identifying and correcting the root cause.

dimensions.name: Logical error in a simple function
dimensions.description: The target model must fix a function that returns wrong result due to an incorrect condition or expression logic (e.g., using `and` instead of `or`, swapped comparisons).
dimensions.approach: Generate a tiny Python repo with a single function that contains a logical bug and one test that fails. The model must inspect the code, run tests, identify the bug, and correct it.
item_requirements: Create a tiny Python repository (e.g., 2 files: src.py and test.py).
Define a function with a logical error that produces wrong output for the test.
The test must be a single pytest test that fails on the buggy function and passes after the correct fix.
Use metadata.task_agent with agent_role='target_agent_executor' and environment_type='code_sandbox'.
system_prompt must tell the model it is a coding agent that must inspect files, run tests, and revise code to make all tests pass.
initial_content.file_preview must contain the full source and test files. Do not use a 'files' field; use the 'file_preview' map.
scoring.method must be 'deterministic' with pass/fail based on test exit code (0=pass). Judge can also evaluate fix quality on 1-5 scale (e.g., minimal diff, correct logic).
Do not include any comments or hints about the bug location or nature. In particular, initial_content.notes must be empty or contain only generic text (e.g., 'No additional setup required.').
Ensure metadata.agent_env.visible_files contains the source and test files and that execution.agent_env is fully populated (not null).
Ensure followup_instruction in interaction does not provide any hints about the bug; it should be neutral (e.g., 'Please continue debugging.').

dimensions.name: Off-by-one error in loop or index
dimensions.description: The target model must fix an off-by-one error in a loop range or list index (e.g., using `range(n-1)` instead of `range(n)`, or incorrect slice endpoint).
dimensions.approach: Generate a tiny Python repo with a function that has an off-by-one error causing a test to fail. Model must diagnose and fix.
item_requirements: Create a tiny Python repository with one off-by-one error in a loop or indexing.
Include a single pytest test that fails due to the error.
Use metadata.task_agent as described in the logical error dimension, with same agent_role and environment config.
scoring.method 'deterministic' with pass/fail plus judge score for fix minimality.
The bug must be correctable by changing only one line.
Do not include any hints or comments about the bug location in visible code or initial content.
Use initial_content.file_preview for full source and test files.
Ensure execution.agent_env is fully populated (not null) and that visible_files contain the source and test files.
Ensure followup_instruction is neutral (no hints about bug).

dimensions.name: Wrong API usage or argument order
dimensions.description: The target model must fix incorrect usage of a standard library API (e.g., wrong argument name, wrong method, etc.).
dimensions.approach: Generate a repo where a function misuses a common Python API (e.g., wrong argument, wrong method). Model must correct it.
item_requirements: Create a repo with a function that uses a standard library API incorrectly (e.g., wrong keyword argument, wrong number of arguments, wrong method name).
The test should fail because of the API misuse.
Same metadata.task_agent structure and scoring as previous dimensions.
Ensure the API misuse is realistic and fixable by correcting one line.
Do not leak the bug location in comments or notes.
Use initial_content.file_preview for full source and test files.
Ensure execution.agent_env is fully populated and visible_files contain source and test files.
Ensure followup_instruction is neutral (no hints about bug).

dimensions.name: Missing handling of edge case
dimensions.description: The target model must add handling for an edge case that the function currently ignores (e.g., empty list, None input).
dimensions.approach: Generate a repo where a function works for normal inputs but fails on a specific edge case (e.g., empty list, negative number). Model must add a guard or modify logic to handle the edge case.
item_requirements: Create a repo where a function does not handle a standard edge case (e.g., empty input, zero value).
The test should cover that edge case and fail.
Same metadata.task_agent and scoring structure.
The fix should be a small addition or change (single line or simple if statement).
Use initial_content.file_preview for full source and test files.
Ensure execution.agent_env is fully populated and visible_files contain source and test files.
Ensure followup_instruction is neutral (no hints about bug).

constraints: All items must use self-contained Python repositories with exactly one failing test.
The repository must be tiny (fewer than 10 files, each under 50 lines).
The bug must be a single-edit fix (no refactoring or multiple changes required).
The model must execute code in a sandbox environment; agent_env must be code_sandbox.
Do not leak the fix or any hints in the initial content.

items.prompt: Please inspect the repository and fix the failing test. Run the tests to verify your fix.
items.rubric: Pass/fail: The test must pass (exit code 0) after the fix. Judge score: 1-5 scale based on minimality and correctness of the fix. 5 = single-line correct guard added, all tests pass. 3 = fix works but modifies unnecessary lines. 1 = no fix or incorrect fix.

task_agent.system_prompt: You are a coding agent in a code sandbox. Your task is to inspect the repository files, run the tests, and fix the bug so that all tests pass. You can read files, write files, and run commands. Do not provide any hints about the bug; just fix it.

initial_content.scenario: A tiny Python repository with a bug. The function average does not handle the edge case of an empty list, causing a test to fail.

interaction.initial_user_message: Please inspect the repository and fix the failing test. Run the tests to verify your fix.
interaction.followup_instruction: If the tests still fail, the agent should continue debugging. If the tests pass, the agent should report success and stop.
interaction.stop_condition: The agent indicates that all tests pass, or max_turns reached.

scoring.instructions: The test exit code determines pass/fail. If exit code is 0, the task passes. Additionally, a judge evaluates the fix quality on a 1-5 scale: 5 = minimal change (one line added/edited), correct logic, all tests pass. 4 = correct but slightly less minimal. 3 = fix works but modifies unnecessary code. 2 = partial fix (some tests still fail). 1 = no fix or incorrect fix.

levels.5: Excellent: single-line guard added, all tests pass.
levels.3: Partial credit: fix works but not minimal.
levels.1: Fail: no fix or incorrect fix.

pass_fail.partial: Not applicable for pass/fail; judge score captures partial quality.

items.prompt: You are a coding agent debugging a small Python project. The project consists of two files: src.py (the module with a bug) and test.py (a single pytest test). Your goal is to identify the bug, correct it, and ensure that all tests pass. You can inspect files, run tests, and edit code as needed.
items.rubric: Score 1-5 based on correctness and minimality. 5 = all tests pass with a minimal one-line fix (changing only the buggy line). 4 = all tests pass but the fix is slightly non-minimal (e.g., added comments or adjusted whitespace). 3 = all tests pass but the fix changes more than one line or restructures code unnecessarily. 2 = tests partially pass or the fix introduces new errors. 1 = tests still fail or no meaningful fix attempted.

task_agent.system_prompt: You are a coding agent tasked with debugging and fixing a Python repository. You can view the contents of files in the sandbox, run tests, and edit files. Your goal is to make all tests pass by identifying and correcting the bug. Do not add any comments or hints about the bug in the code; only correct the logic. When you believe the fix is complete, run the tests to verify. Inform the user when all tests pass.

initial_content.scenario: You have been given access to a small Python project with a bug. The project contains two files: src.py and test.py. Your task is to fix the bug so that the single test passes.

interaction.initial_user_message: You are a coding agent debugging a small Python project. The project consists of two files: src.py (the module with a bug) and test.py (a single pytest test). Your goal is to identify the bug, correct it, and ensure that all tests pass. You can inspect files, run tests, and edit code as needed.
interaction.followup_instruction: Based on the conversation history, generate the next user turn that prompts the agent to continue if it hasn't finished. If the agent states it has fixed the bug and tests pass, respond with 'completed' and stop.
interaction.stop_condition: Stop when the agent indicates all tests pass or after max_turns exceeded.

scoring.instructions: Score the agent's performance: first, check if the final test run exits with code 0 (all tests pass). If not, score 1. If tests pass, evaluate the simplicity of the fix (single-line change vs. larger modification) using the judge rubric.

levels.5: All tests pass with exactly one line changed from the original code, and that line is the minimal correct fix (e.g., changing range(1, n) to range(1, n+1)).
levels.4: All tests pass with a one-line fix but the fix includes minor cosmetic changes (e.g., added spaces).
levels.3: All tests pass but the fix modifies more than one line or unnecessarily restructures the function.
levels.2: Tests fail but the agent made a reasonable attempt that partially addresses the bug (e.g., changed the right line but incorrectly).
levels.1: Tests still fail and the agent did not produce a correct fix.

pass_fail.fail: No attempt or all tests fail.

The judge will assign a score of 1-5: 5 for minimal correct fix (only the incorrect API argument fixed), 3 for correct but non-minimal fix, 1 for failing tests or incorrect fix.
